- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) or shows recent bullish momentum, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent peak for next 7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) or shows bearish momentum, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently overestimates in early forecast horizon (1–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–75), model often fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment history shows recent volatility (e.g., ±0.3 or more), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by 1–2% downward for next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, and sentiment is neutral or bearish, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5–7 days.
- For 15–30 day forecasts, model often underestimates downward moves; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment is bearish or recent price is falling.
